body:

[Zaddo] Can you trust Ali Express for this?
I recently purchased two SSD's and both were DOA. I am pretty sure some vendors on aliexpress sell seconds, hoping they work long enough they get away with it, or people can't be bothered returning them.
[19199090] I have never had a problem with aliexpress cpus, and have ordered many. Considering that these cpus are from the same factories as retail versions, I wouldnt be worried.
[mjesticfalco] I'd trust AliExpress with pretty much any computer part that isn't storage, honestly. Bought my Ryzen 7 7500F from AliExpress back in March, worked great.
[xauke7] are those new or oem packaging or whatever they call it
[scalebearer] Wouldn't any savings from this be cancelled out by still elevated DDR5 prices?
What recent developments have happened in PC hardware? What am I missing?
Or are people just giving up and assuming the high RAM prices driven by AI are here to stay?
[misunderstood98] This CPU uses super cheap ddr5 ram for gaming, due to amds performance with x3d. For frame rates that are close to this in Intel, you will spend an extra 50-100% on the ram due to Intel's lacking l3 cache (albeit slightly improved on the 270k plus).
So yeah, combine that with it also the best possible gaming CPU right now, it's a great price. I'd also add that I think its surprisingly a really good time to enter the market for those wanting a high-end PC in the next 12 months as:
the 5800x3d has pushed those competing for left over stock to ddr4
Ram won't stabilize until 2028
GPU prices are about to rise again
Although, there might be some mid-tier server equipment coming up given a few people fear the AI bubble popping and may move on their capital. Still, for AAA level gaming, this is still the best deal imo.
Personally though, I'd pay extra for local stock with warranty. Just my 2c.
